title: Keyword and context scoring
description: Sensitive keywords (diagnosis, salary, password) contribute base scores, and surrounding context adjusts them: 'password' near 'reset instructions' scores lower than near 'is hunter2'. Weighted scoring beats keyword lists because context disambiguates. Thresholds turn scores into labels. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers keyword base scores adjusted by context.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: "the password reset instructions", 2: "my password is hunter2", 3: "patient diagnosis: diabetes"}
text = CFG[LEVEL]
score = 0
if "password" in text: score += 40
if "diagnosis" in text or "patient" in text: score += 70
if "reset instructions" in text: score -= 25
if "is " in text and "password" in text: score += 30
label = "sensitive" if score >= 50 else ("review" if score >= 20 else "clean")
print("text:", text, "| score:", score, "->", label)
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Data-type inference
description: Columns of data are classified by sampling their values: names, addresses, dates of birth, and identifiers each have characteristic shapes. Inferred types drive default protection: a column inferred as 'email' is treated as personal data until proven otherwise. Inference confidence gates automatic action. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers sampling values to infer column types.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: ["amy", "bob", "cara"], 2: ["amy@x.com", "bob@y.org"], 3: ["1990-01-02", "1985-12-31"]}
import re
vals = CFG[LEVEL]
def infer(v):
    if re.fullmatch(r"[\w.]+@[\w.]+", v): return "email"
    if re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", v): return "dob"
    if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z]+", v): return "name"
    return "unknown"
types = {infer(v) for v in vals}
print("values:", vals, "| inferred:", types)
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Multi-label classification
description: One item can carry several sensitivity labels at once: a medical email is both 'health' and 'contact-info'. Labels are independent, each with its own confidence, and protection is the union of what each label requires. Multi-label output matches how real data mixes concerns. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers independent labels per sensitivity dimension.
